payload.title: Tactus procedures: author, edit, test, schedule and run agent procedures with skills
payload.description:
Make Tactus procedures the working way a Papyrus publication runs repeatable agent work, end to end: write a procedure, edit it in the newsroom, give its agents skills, test it before it runs for real, schedule it or trigger it from a monitor, run it in the cloud, and inspect every run. The basic framework exists but has not been exercised by real work; this initiative finds and fixes the gaps by using it.

Test case: Distinctive Mark's TTAB ruling analysis. When a new Board decision arrives, an agent reads the opinion, classifies it (precedential, notability, issue), writes the ruling page to the publication's editorial context (fetched from the backend at run time, never hard-coded), verifies every fact and pin cite against the opinion, runs the Humanus editorial checks, saves a draft version with the opinion linked as a reference, and stops for an editor's approval before publishing. The same skill document is used by Claude Code interactively and handed to the Tactus agent, so the two stay one procedure.

Principle (Ryan, 2026-10-21): the publication exists to create these problems so Papyrus has to solve them. Prefer fixing Papyrus over working around it, and record each gap found as an issue under this initiative.

Done when: the TTAB ruling-analysis procedure runs on a schedule (or from the TTAB monitor) in the cloud, produces a draft that passes the editorial checks, waits for approval, and its runs can be inspected and re-run from the newsroom and the CLI.
